alegoria-del-trabajo-y-alegoria-de-la-construccion

Two panels show workers building and creating, in a bold, simple style. Saturnino Herrán was a Mexican painter who wanted to celebrate Mexico's own people and history instead of copying European art. He died young, at 31, in 1918. His works helped inspire the great muralists who came after him.
the-offering

An Indigenous couple in a boat of marigolds in the canals of Xochimilco, carrying flowers for the Day of the Dead. Saturnino Herrán painted 'La ofrenda' in 1913, and it is one of the best-known paintings about Mexican traditions. The bright orange cempasúchil flowers guide the spirits home. It's a loving picture of how Mexicans remember their families.
el-gallero

A man in a hat sits and holds his rooster, a fighting cock, ready for a match. Saturnino Herrán painted the ordinary people of Mexico, including farmers and workers, as heroes. The bold shapes show his love of Mexican folk life. It's a proud portrait of a Mexican tradition.
tehuana

A woman from the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in southern Mexico wears the beautiful, embroidered dress and headdress of her region. Saturnino Herrán celebrated Mexican folk culture in his paintings. The Tehuana dress later became famous because Frida Kahlo wore it. It's a colorful portrait of Mexican heritage.
el-cofrade-de-san-miguel

A man dressed as a confraternity member for a holy festival, with a serious face and a colorful costume. Saturnino Herrán painted the traditions of Mexican village life with respect. His paintings gave his country pride in its own faces and customs. It's an example of his last works.
votive-offering

A woman holds a candle and a small offering in a quiet church or chapel, with a golden glow. Ángel Zárraga, a Mexican painter who lived in Paris, painted this in 1912, blending Mexican themes with European modern styles. The soft light and strong shapes make a peaceful scene. It's a thoughtful picture of faith.
summer-fun

Children play and splash on a sunny shore in Sweden, painted in glowing summer light. Anders Zorn, one of Sweden's most celebrated painters, was famous for watercolors and for showing sparkling light on water. He loved to paint his country's countryside and its people. It's a cheerful summer scene.
omnibus

A crowd of passengers sit on a Paris omnibus, which is a horse-drawn bus, with tired faces and lamps burning. Anders Zorn painted this scene of city life, with great skill at catching light. It's a snapshot of daily travel in the 1890s. It's a lively slice of Paris.
a-portrait-of-the-daughters-of-ramon-subercaseaux

Two sisters in white dresses sit together in a bright room. Anders Zorn painted the daughters of a Chilean diplomat living in Paris. His quick, clear brushstrokes make the white dresses glow. It's a charming portrait of sisters.
midsummer-dance

Villagers in folk costumes dance outdoors on a summer evening in the Swedish region of Dalarna, with a golden light and music. Anders Zorn painted this in 1897, and it became one of Sweden's most loved paintings. Midsummer is the biggest holiday in Sweden. It's a happy picture of dancing under the northern sun.
valdemar-atterdag-holding-visby-to-ransom

The Danish king Valdemar Atterdag sits in front of piles of treasure, in 1361, after conquering the Swedish town of Visby on the island of Gotland, while the townspeople bring gold and silver to ransom the town. Carl Gustaf Hellqvist painted this dramatic scene in 1882. It shows a dark day in the history of Gotland. It's one of the most famous Swedish history paintings.
coronation-of-gustav-iii

Gustav III, the king of Sweden, is crowned in a grand ceremony in 1772, in the Storkyrkan church in Stockholm, with a crowd of nobles around him. Carl Gustaf Pilo began the large painting but died before it was finished. The picture shows a bright, glittering moment in history. It's an important picture of Swedish royalty.
gustav-vasas-intag-i-stockholm-1523

The king Gustav Vasa rides into Stockholm in 1523 on a white horse, welcomed by crowds, when Sweden became independent from Denmark. Carl Larsson painted this huge mural in 1908 for the National Museum. Swedes celebrate this event as the founding of modern Sweden. It's an important national painting.
bringing-home-the-body-of-king-karl-xii-of-sweden

Soldiers carry the body of the Swedish king Karl XII through the snow after he was killed in battle in Norway in 1718. Gustaf Cederström painted the sad procession with great drama. The painting is dark and solemn. It's one of the most famous Swedish history paintings.
venny-soldan-brofeldt-artist

A young woman artist in a white blouse looks out confidently. Hanna Hirsch-Pauli, a Swedish painter, painted her friend Venny Soldan-Brofeldt, a Finnish artist. The two women were friends in the art colony in France. It's a portrait of friendship between women artists.
breakfast-time

A mother and her children sit around a sunny table for breakfast in a bright room. Hanna Hirsch-Pauli, a Swedish painter, painted this warm family scene in 1887. The glowing sunlight and morning mood are charming. It's one of the most famous paintings by a Swedish woman artist.
thor-s-fight-with-the-giants

The mighty Norse god Thor swings his hammer at a crowd of giants in a stormy mountain scene, riding in his chariot pulled by goats. Mårten Eskil Winge painted this thrilling picture in 1872, based on Norse myths. It's one of the best-known paintings of Norse gods in Sweden. It's an action-packed fantasy.
launching-the-boat-skagen

Fishermen push a boat into the sea from the beach at Skagen, in the bright light of the north. Oscar Björck, a Swedish painter, spent time with the artists' colony in Skagen. The scene shows real work by the shore. It's a lively picture of fishing life.
nordic-summer-s-evening

Two women sit by a calm bay in the soft, pale light of a Nordic summer night, when the sun hardly sets. Richard Bergh, a Swedish painter, painted this in 1899 to capture the dreamy mood of the northern evening. The still water and the glowing sky are magical. It's one of the most beautiful Swedish landscapes.
aino-myth

In the Finnish epic poem the Kalevala, the maiden Aino is pursued by the old hero Väinämöinen, in a three-part painting. Akseli Gallen-Kallela painted this triptych in 1891, inspired by Finland's national legends. The painting is full of Finnish forest and lake scenery. It is a key work of Finnish national art.
the-defense-of-the-sampo

Warriors fight off an eagle and storm clouds to defend a magical mill called the Sampo, in a scene from Finland's national epic the Kalevala. Akseli Gallen-Kallela painted this in 1896 in a tempera style. The swirling shapes are full of energy. It's an exciting picture of Finnish myth.
kullervo-cursing

The hero Kullervo, in a rage, stands in a stormy landscape and curses his fate, in a scene from the Finnish Kalevala. Akseli Gallen-Kallela painted this dramatic picture in 1899. Kullervo is a tragic figure in the Finnish epic. It's a powerful painting from Finnish national romanticism.
queen-blanche

The medieval Queen Blanche of Namur sits in quiet thought in a castle courtyard in the 1300s, with her young son. Albert Edelfelt, a famous Finnish painter, painted her with great emotion. It's a gentle history painting. It helped make him famous.
burnt-village

A soldier lies near a village that has been burned in a war, with the sky full of smoke. Albert Edelfelt painted a scene from the Finnish War of 1808–1809. The painting shows the sadness left behind. It's a famous early work of Finnish painting.
the-luxembourg-gardens-paris

Children and nannies play in the sunny Luxembourg Gardens in Paris, with fountains and trees. Albert Edelfelt, who studied and worked in Paris, painted it in 1887. The garden is full of bright light and happy kids. It's a cheerful Parisian scene by a Finnish painter.
burning-the-brushwood

A woman and a child tend a fire of brush in a field in Finland, with smoke curling up in the evening light. Eero Järnefelt painted this in 1893, showing traditional slash-and-burn farming. It is one of Finland's best-loved paintings. The glowing smoke and soft sky are lovely.
road-in-hame

A quiet road winds through the Finnish countryside of Häme, with trees and a big sky. Werner Holmberg was a Finnish landscape painter who studied in Düsseldorf. He died young, at 31. It's a calm view of rural Finland.
efterarsmorgen-ved-sortedamssen

A quiet autumn morning along a lake in Copenhagen, with the soft light on the water and a few people along the shore. Christen Købke, a Danish Golden Age painter, painted this view of Sortedam Lake in 1838. The cool air is nearly felt. It's one of the most beloved Danish paintings.
a-burial-mound-from-ancient-times-by-raklev-on-refsns

An ancient burial mound sits in a field by the sea, with a big sky above. Johan Thomas Lundbye, a Danish Golden Age painter, loved to paint old monuments in the countryside. He died young at 29. It's a quiet, thoughtful picture of history in the landscape.
amalienborg-square-copenhagen

The palace square in Copenhagen is nearly empty, in the gray light, with the statue in the center. Vilhelm Hammershøi, a Danish painter, painted quiet, still scenes in muted colors. His pictures feel like holding your breath. It's a calm view of a royal place.
dust-motes-dancing-in-sunbeams

Sunlight streams into a quiet room and lights up the dust floating in the air, with a woman standing in the light. Vilhelm Hammershøi painted his own home in Copenhagen with soft grays and a calm mood. The glowing sunbeam is simple and magical. It's one of his best-known paintings.
peasant-coffin

Farmers carry a coffin on a cart through the snowy countryside, with mourners following. Aleksander Gierymski, a Polish painter, painted this very serious scene to show the lives of the poor with honesty. The cold colors add to the sadness. It's a famous Polish realist painting.
alexander-the-great-trust-to-physician-phillip

Alexander the Great calmly drinks medicine given to him by his doctor Philip, even though he has been told that it may be poison. Henryk Siemiradzki, a Polish painter in Rome, shows the king's trust in a friend. The picture is about courage and loyalty. It's a famous history painting.
christ-and-sinner

Jesus speaks to a crowd that has gathered in a sunny Mediterranean town, with a woman at the center. Henryk Siemiradzki painted this in 1873 in his bright Roman style. The sunlight and architecture are very clear. It's an important Polish religious painting.
the-girl-or-the-vase

A rich Roman man looks closely at two things, a pretty young woman and a fine vase, at a market in ancient Rome, as a merchant waits for his answer. Henryk Siemiradzki painted this funny scene of choosing. The bright Roman light and details are excellent. It's a witty and charming picture.
cranes

A flock of cranes flies across a wide sky over a marsh, in a soft, cold light. Józef Chełmoński, a Polish painter, was famous for painting birds and the Polish countryside. He loved wide landscapes and wild animals. It's a beautiful picture of migration.
gossamer

A young girl with geese walks through a field of tall grass in the golden light of early autumn, with silvery spider threads floating in the air. Józef Chełmoński painted this in 1875, and Poles call it 'Babie lato' (Indian summer). It is one of Poland's most beloved paintings. The glowing light is magical.
storks

A family of storks stands in a field, with their tall nest on a rooftop and the open countryside around them. Józef Chełmoński painted these birds, which are loved in Poland as a symbol of good luck. White storks come to Poland every summer. It's a charming picture of a national favorite.
the-japanese-parisian

A fashionable Parisian woman in a colorful kimono sits among Japanese objects, a big fan and a screen. Alfred Stevens, a Belgian painter in Paris, painted the trend for all things Japanese in the 1870s. The painting is a fun look at a fashion craze. It's an elegant portrait.
jeanne-kefer

A young woman in a white dress looks calmly out of the frame. Fernand Khnopff, a Belgian Symbolist painter, painted the portrait of Jeanne Kéfer, a young girl. He is known for his dreamy, mysterious style. The portrait is both elegant and strange.
i-lock-my-door-upon-myself

A woman sits in a dark room with her face turned away, with a lyre and a closed door. The title comes from a poem by Christina Rossetti. Fernand Khnopff painted this in 1891, a mysterious picture about being alone with your thoughts. It's one of the most famous Belgian Symbolist paintings.
episode-of-the-september-days-1830-on-the-grand-place-o

Fighters in the Belgian Revolution of 1830 rush across the Grand Place in Brussels, flags flying, with a wounded man on the ground. Gustaaf Wappers painted the dramatic and patriotic scene five years after the revolution. It helped inspire Belgians as they built a new country. It's a big Romantic history painting.
the-intrigue-ensor

A group of grinning people in masks and costumes crowd a small room, with strange, funny faces. James Ensor painted the masks of carnival in Ostend, Belgium, when he was young. He found masks to be both fun and creepy. It's an early, striking picture.
the-ironer

A woman irons clothes in a room full of color, painted in bold strokes. Rik Wouters, a Belgian artist, painted his wife Nel at everyday work in his home. The picture glows with bright, happy colors. It's one of the most beloved Belgian paintings.
portrait-of-marguerite-van-mons

A girl in a white dress with a big bow stands in a garden. Théo van Rysselberghe, a Belgian painter, made this portrait using the tiny dots of color of pointillism. The dots make the light sparkle. It's a lovely portrait of a child.
maria-sethe

A woman in a white dress sits in a sunlit garden, as if she is reading. Théo van Rysselberghe painted Maria Sèthe, who later became the wife of the Belgian architect Henry van de Velde. The picture is made of bright dots of color. It's a charming portrait.
a-reading-by-emile-verhaeren

A group of writers and artists gather in a room to listen to the poet Émile Verhaeren read, in the soft light of a lamp. Théo van Rysselberghe painted this group portrait of his friends. Each face has its own personality. It's a picture of friendship and poetry.
golden-summer-eaglemont

A golden Australian landscape of dry grass, gum trees and a faraway blue range of hills, in the heat of summer. Arthur Streeton painted this in 1889 in Eaglemont, near Melbourne, with a group of artist friends. It is one of the most famous Australian paintings. The bright light made it a favorite.
the-purple-noon-s-transparent-might

A wide plain of golden wheat and pale blue shadows stretches out under a huge purple-blue sky on a hot day. Arthur Streeton painted this in 1896, and its title is from a poem by Shelley. He captured the heat and bright light of an Australian summer. It's one of Australia's most loved landscapes.
a-holiday-at-mentone

People relax on the sunny beach at Menton, on the French Riviera, with the blue sea and mountains. Charles Conder, an English-born painter who grew up in Australia, painted this when he was only 20. The bright light and fresh colors are charming. It's an early hit.
the-pioneer

A big three-part painting shows a young pioneer couple in the Australian bush, with the husband swinging an axe, the wife listening to the sounds of the forest, and, in the last panel, a city rising where the forest was. Frederick McCubbin painted this in 1904 to celebrate the settlers. Today, we also ask what the Aboriginal people lost. It's one of Australia's most famous paintings.
anzac-the-landing-1915

Soldiers from Australia and New Zealand climb up a steep cliff under fire at Gallipoli, Turkey, in April 1915, a terrible campaign in World War I. George Lambert, an Australian war artist, painted this big picture after visiting the site. Each year, Anzac Day on April 25 honors these soldiers. It's a solemn and important picture for Australians.
charcoal-burners

Workers burn wood into charcoal in the Australian bush, with the smoke and trees around them. Tom Roberts painted the lives of workers in the bush with great honesty. He was a leader of the Heidelberg School. It's a picture of a hard job.
coming-south

Immigrants on a ship's deck look out at their new home in Australia, as the ship sails into the harbor. Tom Roberts painted this scene of arrival in 1886 after he had made the voyage himself. The excited faces are very expressive. It's a famous picture about the hopes of new settlers.
shearing-the-rams

Men in an Australian woolshed shear sheep, in a busy scene of work, with sunlight streaming through the roof. Tom Roberts painted this in 1890 and it is probably the most famous Australian painting. It shows the hard but proud life of the sheep farms. It's an icon of Australian life.
a-break-away

A horse and rider gallop wildly to turn a stampeding flock of sheep away from a waterhole, in a dust cloud. Tom Roberts painted this in 1891 and the tension is amazing. It shows the dangers of work in the outback. It's a thrilling picture.
bailed-up

A group of bushrangers, outlaws, hold up a stagecoach on a dusty Australian road. Tom Roberts painted this in 1895 based on a real story he'd heard. The mix of danger and adventure was very popular. It's an exciting scene from Australia's wild past.
the-big-picture

Hundreds of people in formal clothes gather in a huge hall in Melbourne in 1901 as the first Parliament of Australia is opened. Tom Roberts spent years painting 269 portraits of the guests. The nickname 'The Big Picture' is well earned, as the canvas is huge. It's a record of the birth of a nation.
proclamation-of-the-republic

Soldiers gather in a square in Rio de Janeiro on November 15, 1889, as Brazil becomes a republic and ends its monarchy. Benedito Calixto, a Brazilian painter, painted the scene a few years later. The celebration was peaceful. It's an image of an important turning point.
the-battle-of-avai

Brazilian soldiers charge across a field in a big and chaotic battle in the Paraguayan War in 1868. Pedro Américo painted this giant picture in 1877. It shows the heroism and the chaos of war. It's one of the largest paintings in Brazil.
independence-or-death

Prince Pedro on horseback raises his sword and declares Brazil's independence from Portugal in 1822, as his guards cheer. Pedro Américo painted this famous scene in 1888. Every Brazilian knows it from school. It's the best-known image of Brazilian independence.
the-first-mass-in-brazil

A group of Portuguese explorers and Indigenous people gather around a big cross at the first Catholic Mass held in Brazil in 1500. Victor Meirelles painted this in 1861 as a founding image of the nation. The Indigenous viewers are shown as curious bystanders. It's one of the best-known paintings in Brazil.
guararapes-battle

Brazilian and Dutch forces fight in a bloody battle in 1649 in the hills near Recife, in a big and chaotic scene. Victor Meirelles painted the battle of Guararapes in 1879. The picture became a symbol for the first national feeling in Brazil. It's an important battle in its history.
a-reading-from-homer

People in a Roman house listen to a reader as he recites the great Greek poet Homer, in a bright marble room with a view of the sea. Lawrence Alma-Tadema, a Dutch-born painter who lived in London, painted ancient life with every marble detail. The picture shows the love of stories that we still share. It's a beautiful scene of ancient culture.
the-women-of-amphissa

Women of the ancient Greek city of Amphissa, tired and asleep in a marketplace after a long festival, are guarded by the heroic women of the town. Lawrence Alma-Tadema based this on a story by the ancient writer Plutarch about women protecting their city. The marble and the sunlight are lovely. It's a scene of courage and kindness.
the-finding-of-moses

An Egyptian princess and her servants find a baby in a basket among the reeds of the Nile, which is the baby Moses. Lawrence Alma-Tadema painted the Egyptian setting in great detail in 1904. The beautiful Egyptian clothes and scenery were carefully studied. It's a famous Bible story painted with archaeological care.
thun-panorama

A huge circular painting shows the whole view of the town of Thun in Switzerland and the surrounding Alps, as if you are standing in the middle. Marquard Wocher painted this panorama in 1814, and it is one of the oldest surviving panorama paintings in the world. People used to stand in a special building and turn around to see all of it. It's an early kind of virtual reality.
sumpflegende

A swamp full of strange plants, shapes and creatures in a dreamy, watery landscape. Paul Klee, a Swiss-German painter, painted the picture as a small, playful world made of lines and colors. His art feels like a fairy tale or a game. It's a fun picture to explore.
twittering-machine

Four little birds perch on a wire attached to a crank, and they seem to sing as the handle turns. Paul Klee painted this strange machine in 1922. It might be a joke about how machines can imitate nature, or a bit scary. It hangs in the Museum of Modern Art in New York, and kids often love it.
senecio

A round face made of circles, squares and triangles with big eyes and a pink-orange cheek. Paul Klee painted this in 1922, and the name 'Senecio' comes from a plant that means 'old man.' It looks like a clown or a mask. It's one of his most famous pictures.
ecce-homo

Jesus is shown to the crowd by Pontius Pilate in a bright, dramatic scene in Jerusalem. Antonio Ciseri, a Swiss-Italian painter, painted this famous work with great realism. It is a very well-known picture in Italy. It's a dramatic Bible scene.
love-at-the-fountain-of-life

A young couple and an angel stand among rocks and trees by a spring of water, in a dreamy, symbolic picture. Giovanni Segantini, an Italian painter who lived in the Alps, painted many pictures about life and nature. The fountain of life stands for the beginning of love. It's a quiet, thoughtful picture.
telemachus-and-the-nymphs-of-calypso

The young Telemachus, son of the hero Ulysses, is surrounded by nymphs who have set his boat on fire, in a scene from Greek myth. Angelica Kauffman, a famous woman painter in the 1700s, painted this story in her graceful style. The soft colors and flowing robes are elegant. It's a lovely picture of ancient myth.
the-sorrow-of-telemachus

Telemachus sits and weeps, missing his father, while the nymphs try to comfort him. Angelica Kauffman, who was Swiss and lived in Rome and London, painted this tender scene. It is part of the story of the Odyssey. It's a picture about longing for family.
thor-battering-the-midgard-serpent

The god Thor swings his hammer at the giant sea serpent, which rises from the ocean, in a dramatic myth. Henry Fuseli painted this thrilling Norse myth in 1790, when few artists painted Norse subjects. The monster coils up in a dark sky. It's an exciting and dramatic picture.
the-mancorbo-canal-in-the-picos-de-europa

A steep, rocky gorge with a rushing river rises between the high peaks of the Picos de Europa in northern Spain, with a stormy sky. Carlos de Haes, a Spanish painter born in Belgium, helped introduce realistic landscape painting to Spain. He made this picture of the mountains after a visit in 1876. It's a famous landscape of northern Spain.
